questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Query plans and performance checks”?
options: Start with a small, readable SELECT query; connect it to an application only after you understand its result.
The plan shows how the student_id lookup is performed; index use depends on the data and optimizer.
SQLite often runs inside the application; MySQL and PostgreSQL commonly run as separate server processes.
The query returns Ada and 42 in two columns.
questions.answer: The plan shows how the student_id lookup is performed; index use depends on the data and optimizer.
questions.explanation:
The plan shows how the student_id lookup is performed; index use depends on the data and optimizer.
Why: When a query is slow, measure it on a small representative dataset before investigating its plan. `EXPLAIN` shows the operations selected by the DBMS; use `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN` in SQLite and `EXPLAIN` in PostgreSQL and MySQL. A plan may reveal a full table scan, index lookup, or join strategy. Appropriate indexes on filter/join columns, refreshed statistics with `ANALYZE`, and avoiding unnecessary rows and columns can help. Plan output can change between engine versions, so do not parse it as a stable application format.
